quest.title: To Whence the Smoke Drifts
quest.description: Citlali comes as promised, but she also makes a request: she wants you to help her find her missing grandson, Ororon. You take this commission and set out alongside her.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This is the spot.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: An eyewitness claimed to have seen Ororon speaking to some Fatui soldiers here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I don't know how much you're willing to believe me... but Ororon really is a good kid. I see no reason why he'd suddenly get involved with the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm convinced that what the witnesses saw was actually the Fatui coercing him, or perhaps trying to extract information.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...However, I doubt anyone would believe me, given there are no signs of a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Didn't Kinich say that she's a big name in Natlan? Feels kinda weird to see her so frustrated and helpless like this...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell us a little more about him?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ororon? Well... He was left at the side of the road as an infant and the people of the tribe took him in. You could say that everyone had a hand in raising him.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He learned a lot from us, and once he reached adulthood, he built himself a house out in the countryside. He spends most of his days growing vegetables and raising Aphids, living off of what he harvests from the garden.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh* He's always been such a good kid. He would even get his friend to deliver whole bags of fresh produce to my place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If that's all there is to him, then he really doesn't sound like a bad person.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah well, let's keep looking. He can answer all of our questions once we find him.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He's been raising Phlogiston Aphids for a long time, and since they were disturbed, they secreted a special type of phlogiston. We can use that substance to track his movements.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's follow the phlogiston trail.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What trail? Paimon doesn't see anything...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah, right, I forgot your eyes don't naturally perceive such things.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Here, give me your hand.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: How about now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you see?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can see the trail now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Paimon can see it now, too!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's right, I used a spell to temporarily transfer a portion of my senses to you. For a short while, you'll be able to see the phlogiston, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you can even share your senses with us? First time Paimon's heard anything like that.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #It requires a very rare spell that most people aren't adept at, but don't worry, it's a cinch for me. Between the two of you, it seems that {NICKNAME}'s senses are a bit stronger than Paimon's.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: When I held your hand just now, I could sense that you've got a great affinity for phlogiston. You're extraordinarily gifted.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, we'll need to use our vision now to track down Ororon. Good luck, you two.

(What does she mean by "deep and confusing"? As far as elderly shamans go, I'd say that I'm already pretty easy to talk to... Is there any other old hag who's as fluent in the language of the youth as me?)
(Hmm, but is my way of speaking still not trendy enough? I've already tried my best to match their speech patterns. But, given the looks on their faces just now...)
(Or perhaps I'm still not fashionable enough? But that can't be, right? Ugh, don't tell me they're still getting the impression that I'm super old-fashioned...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Huh?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I think I just heard a voice... Wait, but it wasn't with my ears... was it all in my mind?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Was that... Citlali's voice?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Seems Paimon heard the same voice, but she also looks like she understood what's going on... Let me think... Ah! It must be a side effect of the spell she cast.)
(Now that I think about it, it's a good thing I found some helpers this time. Some things are best done with the help of friends.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So we can now hear her thoughts through telepathy? Wow, this is amazing! Something like this could only happen with Citlali!)
(Oh? They appear to be feeling quite confident. Looks like our work will go smoothly.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You bet! Just leave it to us.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yep, judging from Paimon's experience as a guide, it definitely looks like people set up camp here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Wait... The phlogiston here is a bit odd.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sees a small shape here. Could it be... some sort of symbol?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This is a distress signal for the Masters of the Night-Wind... Only someone from our tribe would recognize it. So, Ororon was indeed being threatened.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We've got to find him, fast.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Leaving such a subtle mark implies that he was trying to be discreet. In other words... he was probably under the Fatui's watch.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (If they notice us, we can just charge in and fight them to the death. But... But what if my darling grandson is also there? I can't have him caught in the crossfire...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Ugh, no, I've got to be careful, otherwise he'd get hit as well... Ahh, how annoying! No, no, I've got to stay calm, and keep my composure...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are traces of people staying here, too!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Wait a second, the phlogiston around here is jumbled up...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I can also smell a mix of elements in the air. Pyro, Electro... and some other elements as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich told us that you were super amazing! No wonder you can sense so many more things than us!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Hmph, it's about time that little brat said something nice about me.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: There are signs of a struggle here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Judging from what's left on the scene, there must have been a fight. But after that, the factions seem to have gone their separate ways. Both the phlogiston and the elemental traces in the air support that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems like Ororon found a chance to fight back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you still remember the little mark we found before? Paimon's thinking, what if Ororon wanted to leave another distress signal, but was caught by the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Citlali looks pretty worried...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Indeed, judging by the distress signal from before, Ororon was being held by the Fatui. So... given the difference in numbers, he probably wouldn't have been able to overpower them.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Given there are two signals leading from here, we should split up as well.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'll take this direction, and leave the other one to you. Let's meet up again later.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Ororon, what the heck were you doing!? It's one thing to trouble me, but now I had to bring other people into this as well! You little brat!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And off she goes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, did you hear all of that as well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once Citlali left, that voice went away as well... Paimon even tried calling her name inside Paimon's head, but there was no response.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the telepathy doesn't go both ways?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you were thinking the same thing! Paimon also thought that if we could hear what she was thinking, then she could probably also hear what we were thinking in our heads.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think Citlali noticed anything...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She did say that she was quite adept at this spell, and it doesn't sound like she's had any trouble with it in the past... Maybe we're a special case and can hear her thoughts as a side effect?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahaha, if you think about it, she's really got a lively inner world... It paints quite a different picture from Paimon's first impression of her!

talks.objective: Continue investigating the clues in the area
Check the remaining traces at the scene

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There are traces of phlogiston here, but...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you find something?

choices.text: I found some traces of phlogiston.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. So we can't tell where Ororon might have gone from here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's weird! The phlogiston trail suddenly stops. We can't make anything of these footprints, either...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But he can't have just evaporated into thin air, right? We know he wasn't alone. He had all those Fatui with him...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon's right. This is all extremely strange. Also...)
(...So, you can hear the sounds of the wind from beneath the earth.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh!? Whose voice was that just now...?)

choices.text: But the trail completely ends here.

talks.objective: Check the remaining traces at the scene

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Night Kingdom!? How did I get here?)
I'm very sorry, but please do not move. I have no desire to hurt you.
I apologize that our first meeting has to take place like this... It's just that, you're much like one of those animals with ears that perk up as soon as it senses danger in their environment.

And given your combat proficiency, I would not have been able to gain an advantage over you if we were anywhere else in the world. However, you're now in the Night Kingdom, a familiar domain to the Masters of the Night-Wind.
Hello, Traveler. I am Ororon, the one you've been searching for.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...But what does this mean? Have you escaped the Fatui's custody?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ah... The Fatui's custody. I see, so even Granny has told you that I was coerced by the Fatui. I'm afraid you've been brought here by a lie, like a false omen in the lingering smoke.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: My friend and I only left those traces to lure you here. Deceiving you was never our true intent, however. It was simply... the fastest and most feasible way for us to set up a meeting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's... The Captain!?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Greetings, Traveler from afar.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #{M#Be careful with this Traveler. His soul is temporarily restrained by us and appears to have become more fragile in the process. It's taking all my concentration to hold onto him.}{F#Be careful with this Traveler. Her soul is temporarily restrained by us and appears to have become more fragile in the process. It's taking all my concentration to hold onto her.}

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: It was I who tasked Ororon with leaving the traces to lead you here, and I who used the Masters' ritual to bring your soul to the Night Kingdom.

choices.text: So, you are working together.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I've heard much about you from the past encounters you've had with my colleagues. Given the present situation in Natlan, I would like to sincerely request a formal meeting with you... in person.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I will use the opportunity to explain my goals and motivations to you, as well as why I mistrust Mavuika, the Pyro Archon. I believe there is little reason for you to blindly follow her plan.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: If you would like to hear our intel, then find us to the east of the Stadium. But remember, not a word of this to anyone. I would like to avoid any further conflict.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: You will see me again once you return to reality. No matter what I say, please help me keep this a secret. This is all to avoid dragging Granny into this conflict.

choices.text: What do you want?

talks.objective: Check the remaining traces at the scene

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what happened just now!? You suddenly collapsed and stopped responding!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah... I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Was my soul forcibly removed from my body just now? That would explain why I couldn't hear Paimon at all.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, why are you sitting on the ground? Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Citlali! {M#He}{F#She} froze for a moment and then just collapsed to the ground...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Could it have been those leftover remnants from the Night Kingdom? Do you have any itches or pain anywhere?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm fine, just a little lightheaded.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we can take a short break. Sorry, I know I asked for your help... but had I known you were feeling unwell, I wouldn't have taken you on this trip with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If they were being truthful, then they must have reasonable motivations for what they did. But should I trust them?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I could just share everything with Paimon and Citlali right now, but that'd mean giving up on the lead. I still haven't had much dealings with either the Fatui or the Masters of Night-Wind... I suppose I'll stay quiet for now, and see if I can find out anything else.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you're feeling sick, you should just say so! Citlali should be able to, uh, exorcise any ghosts or weird stuff that you picked up in the Night Kingdom!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: A seasoned traveler must know the importance of not pushing yourself beyond your limit. If you need anything from me, just say the word.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, everyone. I'm feeling fine now.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: In any case, let's take a bit more time to rest now.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Even though the situation remains quite urgent, you take a longer break with Paimon and Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ororon's words still echo in your mind. Meanwhile, Citlali continues to keep her eyes on you and even performs another checkup.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Tsk, need to be more careful next time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Feeling better yet, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, let's get ready.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I followed my phlogiston trail earlier to a stronghold guarded by soldiers. I have a feeling that Ororon is probably being held inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so it's close by? Then let's head over right away!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry... I didn't realize I was holding you up...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, I recruited you to be my helper, which means we're in this together. Like the wind and the clouds, we either move as one or not at all.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...But if you want to make it up to me, then just be sure to fight extra hard when the time comes.

talks.objective: Go to the campsite that Citlali found

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Look over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Paimon thinks she sees someone in the middle of the camp!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's Ororon. So he really was taken by the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So, that's Ororon... He does look the same as when I spoke to him in the Night Kingdom earlier.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! We'll take the lead!

dialogues.speaker: Kosterlitzky
dialogues.text: Hey! Quit daydreaming! Don't you have work to do?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...I cannot see the sun.

dialogues.speaker: Kosterlitzky
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Without the sun, I cannot see the truth. You are currently blocking the light, so I must beseech you to move aside.

dialogues.speaker: Kosterlitzky
dialogues.text: Huh? Okay, Mr. Philosopher, that's enough mumbo-jumbo!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Wow... I'm going to rip that guy's head right off!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Citlali's struggling to control her temper now...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph... Are you ready? Let's go kick their butts!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: On my count... Three, two, one!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ororon!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Granny!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Paimon knows she's called Granny Itztli, but it's still kinda weird hearing someone actually call her "Granny"...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #And greetings to you... {M#Gramps.}{F#other Granny.}

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Gramps}{F#Granny}!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What did you just call {M#him}{F#her}!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #{M#Gramps. Is that not right? You're Granny's friend, are you not? You seem to be approximately the same age as her, so I figured you've got to be "Gramps."}{F#Granny. Is that not right? You are Granny's friend, are you not? You seem to be approximately the same age as her, so I figured you're also a "Granny."}

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: How many times have I told you? It doesn't work like that. There are a lot of people who look about the same age as me! You can't go around calling everyone "gramps" or "granny"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait wait wait, he's not a child, is he? Don't tell Paimon he's one of those people who look like an adult but are actually only eight or nine years old!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Your words have pierced my heart like a thorned vine. Given how hard those thorns are to remove, I may just need to find a pair of tweezers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you so upset? You can just say yes or no!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Of course I'm not a child. It's just, Granny always taught me to show gratitude where it's due. And since the Masters of the Night-Wind raised me collectively, I basically see everyone above a certain age as an elder I should look up to.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The way he talks has definitely changed, but it doesn't feel like he's putting on an act. He asked me to do whatever I could to help keep things a secret, and even said it'd be for Citlali's sake...)

choices.text: So you treat everyone like they're your Uncles and Aunties?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Exactly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, but if you keep that up, then everyone's going to be your senior...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: And do you think saying all of this is gonna save you from a scolding, Ororon?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Haven't I told you a hundred times since you were a kid? Heed the three warnings!

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Be wary of beasts prowling around, scammers looking for their next victim, and strange people who appear out of nowhere.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh, so you do remember, and you just chose to ignore them! I always knew that living on your own was going to get you into trouble sooner or later, but getting kidnapped? That really takes the cake!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You won't always be able to rely on other people coming to your rescue, you know! You're just lucky we got here when we did, or we might be launching another search-and-rescue operation to find out where they put your severed head.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'm sorry, Granny. I'll be more careful next time.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Next time!? Ohoho, good one! You think there'll be a next time after this!? Not a chance!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmph... They didn't hurt you, did they?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: No, they just asked me a lot of questions about Natlan's terrain and made me draw a map of the Ley Line distribution.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Okay, now answer me honestly... Were you the one who helped The Captain escape after his battle with the Pyro Archon?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: So why did you do it?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Because...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Because they said they would need my help from there on out. They also said that if I refused, they'd just come to you, Granny, and they'd already figured out a way to make you do their bidding.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hey! I'm no ordinary granny! Would they really dare to come after me? And you! Did the gods give you a brain just for you not to use it? Did you really believe everything they said at face value, and not stop to think?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Thankfully, the Pyro Archon only asked that we find the "mysterious individual from the Masters of the Night-Wind," and didn't slap your name on a wanted poster. Don't think for a second that she doesn't know what's happening.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: "Even if the truth that you see will soon manifest into reality, there is still no need to preemptively panic." Have you forgotten the words that I've taught you?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Hmph. Forget it.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: We can submit the details of this camp and the defeated Fatui as evidence of your innocence.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Let's clean this place up and get back to the city. Ororon, you better remember this lesson well and seriously reflect on your actions. Also, once we return to the city, come to the Speaker's Chamber with me. I'll need you to explain everything.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Sounds good. Should I bring some of my homegrown vegetables as well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your... vegetables?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Yes. I grow a lot of fresh produce in my garden. I hope the Pyro Archon won't be too picky about the selection.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ugh, now's not the time to be thinking about that. If you do come face to face with the Pyro Archon, the first thing you should do is...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Recite the three warnings.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh!? No, you should emphasize that you were not in cahoots with the Fatui!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How exactly did the Masters raise this guy...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Oh... right.

choices.text: So you treat everyone like they're your Gramps and Grannies?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to the city and Citlali brings you to the Speaker's Chamber, where you recount everything that has happened to Ororon.

dialogues.speaker: Coyopa
dialogues.text: ...I see. So Ororon came to The Captain's rescue because he promised to help him in exchange for Citlali's safety.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: That's right. I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Now that you know Ororon was only trying to protect another member of his tribe, could I ask you to petition the Pyro Archon for her forgiveness?

dialogues.speaker: Coyopa
dialogues.text: We will give her a full report. We'll let you know once she has reached a decision.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Will I need to stay here?

dialogues.speaker: Coyopa
dialogues.text: Technically, yes. But if Ms. Citlali is willing to serve as your guarantor, then we can release you from custody.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sure, I'd be happy to do that. I don't have any more time to waste here — I still have other things to do.

dialogues.speaker: Coyopa
dialogues.text: Understood, thank you very much. Mr. Ororon, please report back to the Speaker's Chamber as soon as you've received notice of the Archon's decision.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I understand. Thank you. And thank you too, Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Well, at least you won't need to hide your face anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, thank you very much for your help. And don't worry, I haven't forgotten about my side of the deal.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Once Ororon is settled, I'll go talk to Xilonen and get started on forging an Ancient Name for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll be counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You scratch my back, I scratch yours. It's as good as done — you can just go twiddle your thumbs or something while you wait for the good news. Bye for now.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Come with me, Ororon. We've got to find you a place to stay for the night.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Goodbye, {M#Gramps}{F#other Granny}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This new grandson of mine is way too polite.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That look on his face... He's probably trying to remind me about my promise.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He doesn't strike me as a liar... Had I not seen everything for myself, I'd have never guessed that he could have done so much work behind Citlali's back. What does he really want...?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! We're finally done! Alright, it's time to find some grub...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, there's something I need to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh? What is it, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You pull Paimon aside and tell her everything that you saw earlier when you collapsed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaaat!? The Captain!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Keep your voice down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, sorry! P—Paimon just didn't see that coming! So, you really saw him in the Night Kingdom? And he didn't attack you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, that Ororon... What is he up to? He sounded earnest enough just now, Paimon would've never guessed anything was happening!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All that stuff about protecting Citlali and being forced to help the Fatui... When he's actually been a willing accomplice all along!

choices.text: I'm still not completely sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon appreciates you telling her about this! Paimon will support your choice no matter what, so if you wanna go, we can go together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We still have another whole day before the meeting, so we'll just meet with them when the time comes.

choices.text: We still need more information.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weird, Paimon doesn't see anyone... Ohh, please don't let this be a trap!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek!!! What's that!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Good evening. Nice to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's you! You shouldn't pop up from behind people like that! What're you, a ghost!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm terribly sorry. It's just... a force of habit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, and what's with you apologizing all the time? You sound so polite and honest but you're actually doing shady stuff behind people's backs!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You're right, Granny tells me that too. Huh, come to think of it, you remind me of her... Sometimes you two sound really similar, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're gonna call Paimon granny too, now?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Well... I could.

choices.text: So what's the purpose of this meeting?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: It's all clear. Over to you.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Excellent. The fact that you showed up proves that I was right about your character.

choices.text: I'm only interested in the intel.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Yet, there's been a lot of talk about you. Childe told me that you're passionate about the unknown and willing to take risks. Rather than facing you as an enemy, I would much prefer to bring you to my side.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: If we allow the current state of things to continue, we will inevitably clash, and that's a scenario that I'd very much like to avoid.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I've long heard of your exploits across the nations. Though you have crossed swords with my colleagues many times, I know that you're by no means an unreasonable person.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: And once you've learned the truth that the Pyro Archon, Mavuika, would never willingly share with you, you may just find it in your heart to consider my proposal.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I assume you've already been informed of the Pyro Archon's plan. In order to defeat the Abyss and save Natlan, she still needs two more heroes to appear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, how did you know that!? Uh, never mind, guess that's not important now...

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I've long kept a close eye on her plan. To be frank, it's an exceedingly risky plan. Will the heroes really appear? And even if they come to her, will their power be enough to drive the Abyss back?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: If any part of the plan goes awry, all of Natlan — even all of Teyvat, will pay for her mistakes.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Now, you may have been led to believe that this is the only plan available to her. But what if I told you she's had another emergency plan all along, the details of which she has chosen to keep hidden from you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An emergency plan...?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Yes, a way to keep Natlan intact even if her original plan fails. But given the painful cost of its execution, she has chosen to keep it as a mere backup plan.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Whether this stems from hesitation, fear, or even naivete, I cannot say. But Natlan cannot afford to wait until she comes to her senses.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: My fear is that given the enormity of the decision, she will be reluctant to confront the dire reality we face until it is too late. There will be no time left to execute the backup plan, and all of Natlan will be lost to the Abyss.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: We have to make the decision for her, here and now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's just your speculation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, do you have any evidence for all of this? Just telling us a bunch of scary stuff isn't enough, you know!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, wasn't it you who tried to seize the Gnosis for the Tsaritsa's plan?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, by seizing the Gnosis and "making the decision for her," could he mean that...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Gnosis has something to do with this "backup plan"?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I knew you'd be clever enough to see. That's right — I did not seek to seize the Gnosis for the Tsaritsa.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Since I was defeated in battle, I must put to rest my thoughts about the Gnosis. But even so, my desire to save Natlan remains unchanged.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: And now, I have found a new way to solve the crisis. We can implement it immediately if we reach an agreement...

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: ...Hmph.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Someone's here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? The Captain disappeared!?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Something's rapidly approaching... Oh, no!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: "Something"!? Bad news, chump — it's your Granny!

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Oof!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Citlali! Wh—When did you get here?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmph, I knew something was amiss after we were separated. Hidden ceremonial tools, and an unconscious Traveler... I must say, I'm very curious about what you're up to!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: How dare you go behind our backs like this, Ororon! Colluding with the Fatui? Really?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh, here we go again — cat got your tongue, huh? You really think you can avoid a scolding just by staying quiet?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'm not trying to avoid anything.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oho, and now you're talking back! Well, go on then, explain yourself. What the heck are you up to!?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'm sorry, Granny... I feel so guilty...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You...! That's it, where are my tools!? I swear, if I don't teach you a lesson right here and now, I'll...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah wait, Citlali! Please calm down! We still learned a lot of info, didn't we? Like the fact that The Captain isn't trying to seize the Gnosis anymore!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So maybe just save the scolding for later, okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, this is no place to discipline a child.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Listen well, Ororon. You're only getting out of this now because of the Traveler's plea. This isn't over, you hear me?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #*sigh* You're right, {NICKNAME}. Let's go. We can discuss this more back in the city. You two keep an eye on Ororon for me, okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Our conversation with The Captain was interrupted at the most crucial moment. But if Ororon's still here, maybe we can still learn the rest from him.)

choices.text: I don't really care how the Fatui thinks of me.
Let's get straight to the point.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh! In all my years, I've never had a child cause me so much grief. Do you seriously not see what's at stake here? You've got a head on your shoulders, Ororon! Use it!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Why did you help The Captain? And I want the truth this time!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hah, no answer? Think you're being smart? Then let me ask a different question. What does The Captain want? What is his purpose in Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Really? You're just going to stonewall me!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like Ororon has no intention of answering her...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Just use your brain for a second. What do you possibly stand to gain by helping The Captain? Only endless trouble awaits you and everyone in the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You've always been a good kid, why would you throw that all away now? If you're worried about something, just talk to me. Granny would much rather we had a conversation instead of constantly clashing like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Why is he staring at us all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry that you have to hear all this.

choices.text: Ahaha... It's fine.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: You are very kind. Most people would have fled by now. Not everyone can handle Granny's scolding.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh? You dare gossip between yourselves instead of listening to me!? You...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, sorry! Sorry, Granny...!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmph... "sorry, Granny"... Hehe... hahaha, "sorry, Granny"! You know what, fine! I'm perfectly aware that everything I say goes in one ear and out the other. You're all grown up now, so why would you listen to an old hag like me?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You say all the right things, but then you go and completely ignore me. Well, if that's how you're going to treat me, you can stop sending Ifa over to my place to deliver your stupid vegetables. I don't need anything from you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who's Ifa? A delivery person?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That's irrelevant! The point is, he hangs out with this kid, so he must be no good. Tsk, you kids get to a certain age and suddenly act like you know it all... There's nothing I can say to get through to you.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Ororon, if you're still thinking about that so-called "duty," then please, just forget about it. The Ley Lines did not fall to this state because of you, and we've long closed the book on that incident.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, seems they've started talking about some kind of tribal history? Paimon's starting to get lost...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: That's not it, Granny.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh? There's something off about that voice...)

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I know you tend to get down on yourself when you're upset, but I can tell I've really hurt you this time. All I can say is, I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: His voice... Ororon!? Where have you gone?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds like he's somewhere super far away, but isn't he right here in front of us...?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'm really sorry. It's up to all of us to do everything we can to save Natlan, so I've got to go.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Get back here this instant! Ororon... Ugh, what is this? Powder from plant spores? Is that the trick he used?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What just happened? How was he able to suddenly get so far away like that?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's a trick of his! If you grind spores into a powder and spray it in the air, it can be manipulated to create an illusion...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: He pulled it off flawlessly, he must have put a lot of time into perfecting it. Don't tell me that's how he's been hunting in the fields these days... Couldn't he have picked up something more useful!?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ugh, little brat! That's it! The next time we meet, I'm definitely going to break his legs!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that's a little extreme... But still, why does he feel like he needs to run from us? If his goal is also to protect Natlan, then can't we work together?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He still doesn't want to tell us anything about his goals.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I'm sorry for interrupting your conversation with them earlier. But even if you'd been able to hear them out, there's no guarantee you would have gained anything substantial.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ororon probably did everything he could to get away because he knew I'd get the truth out of him sooner or later. That brat, I swear...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Captain probably has some sort of substantial plan. Otherwise, Ororon would have no reason to keep following him.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Meeting again is out of the cards for now, so it might be faster to just approach the Pyro Archon and confirm what The Captain said. And also...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I can tell that Ororon's stubbornness has hurt Citlali deeply. I need to find a way to comfort her.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was all that about Ororon's "duty" earlier?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: We've got quite a long walk back to the city... let's take our time. It'll give me a moment to figure out how to explain all this.

choices.text: Well, it's definitely a little awkward...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Indeed. It's like going to visit a friend at his house, only to suddenly hear your friend berating a naughty Saurian...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's... an oddly specific analogy! Wait, did one of your friends really do that?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Yes. And every time my friend scolded his Saurians, they would look at me the same way you're looking at me now — helpless and embarrassed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but you're the one getting your head chewed off! Stop making this about us!

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Indeed, you've got a point. Then please just hang in there for a little while longer. Granny should be done with her scolding session soon.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Do you two have some time? Feeling hungry? How about we get something to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! It's been a while since we last ate... Now that we can relax, Paimon just realized how hungry she is!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Then let's go. We can find somewhere to sit down and talk. Food and drinks are on me.

choices.text: It's okay, we can cover our own bill...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Really? You're not gonna take her offer?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Ah, that's right... Citlali has gotten a lot quieter since Ororon ran away. She seems to be having a hard time...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{M#He}{F#She}'s right! We're seasoned adventurers, so we're more than capable of paying our own bill!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hey, come on now? You won't even let me take you out for some food and drinks? *sigh* I just wanted to treat you to a meal...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you sure? We can save you some Mora...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hah, Mora is the least of my concerns. Besides, we're definitely due a meal after all the time we've spent together. Let me get this one — I might be an old hag, but I like to think I'm not completely useless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, that's fine with us, but... Paimon doesn't want you to be sad, Citlali.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Haha, don't worry. I'm sure a juicy grilled steak will work wonders.

choices.text: Paimon's got a secret food fund, so she can do the honors.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? How did this become Paimon's bill?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Aww... Citlali looks quite down on herself.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright, it's on Paimon this time! What's one meal to the best guide in Teyvat?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you can just sit back and enjoy, Citlali! Paimon will take care of it!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The three of you walk into a tavern and find a quiet spot to sit.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon order some food and fruit juice while Citlali begins chugging down bottle after bottle of wine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm? What are you looking at?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Do you see two people standing by the door? They look like spitting images of each other. Are they twins?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon only sees one person there.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh? How could that be... Eh, guess my mind isn't as sharp as it used to be. Get me another bottle, Boss!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, do you think she's drunk?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd be surprised if she wasn't...

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: There you go, Miss! Oh my, it's not every day you see Granny Itztli here with some friends... Not to mention ones who've made a huge name for themselves recently!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? So you've heard of us? Ehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Of course I have. Aren't you the ones who saved Kachina and brought her back? No wonder you hit it off with Granny Citlali — she wouldn't spend time with just anybody, you know. *sigh* I don't even remember the last time I saw her with a new friend...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you call her "Granny," too?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Well, given our ages, it'd probably be more accurate for me to call her my great-great-granny, haha. She's one of the most famous people at the Masters of the Night-Wind — most days, hardly anyone even dares to talk to her!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh? Gossiping about me right in my face now, are you, Chanca?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Please, Granny, I wouldn't dare! I'm just beyond happy to see you bring over some new friends. After all, any friends of our regulars are sure to be great customers, too.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, that's enough. Go on, now, I'm sure other customers would like to talk to you as well. There's no need to keep staring at me — I promise I'll keep my alcohol down until I leave.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Ahahaha. Well then, you have my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After Chanca leaves, Citlali downs a few more glasses and begins to stare blankly into space from her chair.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You start wondering whether she's actually drunk, or working through some complex problem in her head.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali? Citlali!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh... Who's that? Hmph, you got some gall calling me by my first name! *hic* Lemme guess — you wanna test your skills against Granny Itztli, don't ya?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, are you still with us, Citlali? You're kinda talking to no one...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph! You chumps come around here, picking fights with me... Well, you know what happens next? You lose, and then run off home to tell everyone about how I'M this big scary bully... It's always the same story. You brats start it, I finish it, and then I end up with the reputation of being some kind of terrible monster among the shamans...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I mean, c'mon! Monster, me? Really? What did I do to deserve that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Granny Citlali, you're not a monster at all!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Exactly! And while we're at it, I'm not some lazy slacker, either! Between meditation, advising the chief, and speaking with the Wayob, I actually have a pretty packed schedule, y'know...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...*hic*! Oh yeah, AND I have to mentor after all the new kids! Hey, new kid! Yeah, you!

choices.text: Who? Me?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Don't play dumb! Didn't I teach you how to find phlogiston? You see, I know my stuff! I'm a good teacher, you tell 'em!

choices.text: Absolutely!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmph, that's more like it. 'Bout dang time someone showed me a little respect! Yeah, Granny's a hard worker alright... You can always rely on old Granny... *hic*...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Zzz... Zzz...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did she just fall asleep with her eyes open? Oh geez...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Behind this pitch-black curtain, a chapter of hatred reveals itself. Behind the smoke, the lingering smoke...

response.speaker: Chanca
response.text: Ah, she's meditating again! She does this whenever she's had a few too many drinks. Her mind's actually racing at this point — it's quite the opposite of sleep!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this another specialty of the Masters of the Night-Wind?

response.speaker: Chanca
response.text: No, I'd say it's an ability that's unique to Citlali herself. While she can easily pick up everyone else's skills and tricks, few have been able to master hers.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Warning... Warning... Red, the red color of danger... has now arisen within that pair of eyes...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Huh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waaaaaah!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you awake?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon...? I...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I... I'm gonna hurl... Ughhh...

response.speaker: Chanca
response.text: Hang on! Just keep it in!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Phew... Okay, it's passed. That was a close one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You had Paimon worried! Paimon really thought you were about to barf all over the table just now!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ugh, how embarrassing... I'm sorry you had to see me like that. It's never happened before, I swear... I've never thrown up. Not once.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We didn't ask about before...!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you feeling okay? Wanna take a quick walk and get some fresh air?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: There's so much that I want to say, but... I can't.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why not? Of course you can, just say whatever's on your mind.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Please, Paimon, it's not as simple as you think... We've only known each other for a few days, right? What would you think of me if I were to start dumping all my complaints on you after we've only just met?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon gets it! You're hoping that we wouldn't think less of you no matter what you're about to say!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ah? No, that wasn't my point at all! Seriously, don't you youngsters know anything about shame? I'm talking about shame! I've lived all these years and still can't get rid of it... Surely, you know the feeling, too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Actually... About that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Should we just tell her?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh? Tell me what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, this is as good a time as any.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, Citlali...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Listen carefully, and try not to get too upset...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You describe the events that took place during Ororon's rescue as objectively, fairly, and impartially as possible.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Citlali shared some of her senses with you through a spell, allowing you to temporarily hear her thoughts.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: So you heard... you heard my...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, Citlali! You had every right to complain about those things!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I can't take it anymore! Why do these things happen to me?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hearing me mumble under my breath is one thing, but hearing what I mumble in my own head? That's too much...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's just like when you're rolling on the floor in your pajamas, but you forget to lock the door, and someone bursts in to deliver cabbages and sees the whole thing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that, uh... happens to you a lot?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...It happens to people in general, okay!? Doesn't matter if you're two hundred years old or a thousand years old... Everyone rolls around in their pajamas sometimes! I was just picking something... generic...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you okay? You look dejected.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Take a walk with me. I have things to share with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like she's completely given up... like those criminals who just confess everything and accept their fate...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We should follow her, just to make sure she doesn't do anything stupid...

choices.text: Thank you for all your teachings, ma'am!
Guess I'm a "new kid"?

talks.objective: Follow Citlali to a different spot

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well? Great view, right? I love coming here by myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's beautiful!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for bringing us here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Haha, you're making me want to cry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, what do we do? Please don't cry!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It was an expression, okay? A figure of speech! I'm just... embarrassed. Here you are thanking me, even after you helped me all this time...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's just have a casual conversation. It's easiest that way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? You don't seem like the kind of person who keeps things "casual"...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, I guess I used to be more of a stickler for the rules.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And you're right... I don't usually open up to the people of my tribe like this.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm just an eccentric old hag to them. That story's been passed down so long, it might as well be true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, you're just a regular person!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Haha, the kids of my tribe would have a heart attack if they heard you say that... "Granny Itztli is a powerful figure. Be careful around her!" — that's what they'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you ARE powerful. Are they afraid of you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Some are... Others are mad I always come out on top. A few decades like that, and people stop knowing how to deal with you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What about you? Are you scared of me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't find you scary at all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon's right.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph... That's because you're not from my tribe. You don't know how many delusions of grandeur I've destroyed just by existing!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I make people realize that, no matter how hard they work, they'll never become a living legend like me.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Not to brag or anything! Maybe it's hard to believe. Just... just pretend I never said anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We believe you! Xilonen has full faith in your abilities, and Ororon didn't seem scared of you. He thinks of you as his "Granny," right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yes, but Ororon's a special case.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Mavuika already told you about her plan, and you've given so much help to Ororon and me... You deserved to learn the full truth.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ororon's... not like other people. As I mentioned, he was abandoned as a child...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The reason being, his soul is incomplete. The Masters of the Night-Wind view this as a bad omen, capable of bringing about illness and misfortune.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No one knows who his parents were. He was just left on a rock in the wilderness. It's a miracle he wasn't devoured by some wild beast.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Masters of the Night-Wind believe they can see human souls, and in Ororon's incomplete soul, they saw a possibility for Natlan...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: A possibility... to turn Ororon into a vessel for lost souls.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The ceremony would allow lost souls to gather within him. Ororon would then be sent to the Night Kingdom to return the souls to their rightful place, strengthening the Ley Lines and completing the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that doesn't sound right!

choices.text: Sending a living person to the Night Kingdom...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Now, you see the problem.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: When damage occurs to the Night Kingdom, the souls held within disperse and remain adrift, unable to find a way back to the Ley Lines. This loss of souls damages the Night Kingdom even further.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The ceremony can send back countless souls at once, which would benefit the Night Kingdom and the souls themselves. Of course, the vessel, Ororon, would be sacrificed in the process.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I wasn't surprised the chief at the time came up with the plan. The Ley Lines were already in a terrible state. A suitable candidate for the ceremony appears, and now you have the chance to make things better... Of course you're going to take it.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: When the chief asked for my opinion, I didn't give my approval, but I didn't object, either. So, they went ahead with the ceremony... It failed, and Ororon escaped with his life.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Pathetic, isn't it? By not objecting, I basically gave them the go ahead. Maybe they didn't have my explicit approval, but it's not like I did the right thing. If the ceremony was successful, Ororon would probably be dead.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Of course, in my tribe, death is rarely something to fear, but what kind of message would we be sending by sentencing a newborn to death? By using a human life as a tool?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's not right! So, when I learned the ceremony had failed, I was ashamed by my inaction and absolutely relieved by the result.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The plan was never a secret. Or, I guess I should say... there was no point to keeping it a secret. A simple investigation from Ororon would reveal everything.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Everyone thought he would be happy he survived, and he never really said anything to the contrary. But, just as I was about to put all of it behind me...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: He asks this question — "Would Natlan have been saved if the ceremony succeeded?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but... It's not his fault!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: He knows that, but he still feels guilty. Ororon has a strong ability to perceive souls. More than any of us, he understands just how dire the situation with Ley Lines has become.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Maybe he chose to work with the Fatui because he still thinks he owes a debt to Natlan. I can only imagine what they told him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Traveler, didn't The Captain say he found a way to solve the crisis? Maybe that's what brought Ororon into this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, we can't just let things go on like this... We have to convince him to come back!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, that should be our next step.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, you don't look so good, Citlali... Maybe you should head back and get some sleep.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Probably drank too much... It's okay, the fresh air is doing me good...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: *retch* Okay forget that, I need to go home. I hit it a little too hard...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry. You don't have to do any of this alone!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You've helped me so much already. How do I even begin to thank you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, we're friends, aren't we? Besides, you already said you owe us a favor. So, you don't need to worry about us!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Good point... Well, I'll go home and get some sleep. We can figure out our next move in the morning.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: "Friends"... Haha, I like the sound of that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ororon's probably back with The Captain, don't you think?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah. We should tell the Pyro Archon what we learned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean about the "backup plan"? Do you really believe what The Captain told us?

choices.text: She needs to know regardless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. We should just go to her directly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, she's probably asleep. We can find her first thing in the morning. For now, let's... *yawn*... go to bed.

choices.text: We should just be upfront with her.
Wouldn't that just kill him?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmm, don't think there's anything here... How about we check out somewhere else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over here, this way! Hehe, Citlali might say a lot of deep and confusing stuff, but this spell of hers is really something.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What was that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon was just complimenting you! Really!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, looks like there's a new camp over there!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's go take a look.
(That little brat, I swear... I just hope he hasn't gotten himself into any real trouble.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sees some traces here! Let's follow them and see if we can find anything up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Still trying to resist? You've got no idea who you're up against.
